title: Targets at shared chemical synaptic sites had more direct connections than fixed-count controls in eight worm maps
abstract: We tested whether targets at a shared chemical synaptic site also connect directly to each other more often than fixed-count controls predict. We used eight public C. elegans brain maps and a fixed panel of 162 neurons. Within-source trades kept every source-target count and every site target count fixed. The fraction of co-target pair occurrences with a direct chemical edge was 1.41 to 1.56 times the control mean. Every observed primary score exceeded all 998 saved controls for its map. Reciprocal edges, equal source weights and a three-contact threshold gave the same direction. Longer trade spacing and new seeds changed primary control means by less than 0.35 percent. These are conditional anatomical comparisons, not animal confidence limits. Local geometry and physical contact opportunity were not controlled. No neural activity or release coupling was measured. The result shows circuit organization beyond the tested counts in these partial maps; it does not establish a computational benefit. Code, scalar draws, validation, source hashes, a figure and retrieval instructions support reproduction. External records remain outside the bundle.
